target.statement: UCF achieves an Average Precision (AP) of 0.313 ± 0.252 on the 'Small' category of ADBench datasets (N ≤ 1000 and d ≤ 50).
target.dataset: ADBench 'Small' category (datasets with N ≤ 1000 and d ≤ 50)

compute.basis: The UCF method is a lightweight, non-training algorithm that only requires inverting small (n+1)×(n+1) matrices per query point; the 'Small' ADBench datasets are tiny (N ≤ 1000), and the paper reports inference times on the order of 10^-2 seconds per sample, so running 5 repetitions over ~10 small datasets should take well under an hour on a CPU.

blockers: The GitHub repository may not include the exact ADBench data splits or the full experimental configuration (e.g., the specific 5 random seeds and stratified splits), which could cause slight deviations from the reported mean and standard deviation.
title: Scalable anomaly detection via a univariate Christoffel function
